assigned.title: Trusted-proxy topology and how this deployment derives a client IP
assigned.acceptance:
THE HAZARD, AND THE RULING THAT CREATED THIS TASK. PL-0719 found that better-auth keys each rate-limit bucket by client IP and path, and that when it cannot resolve a client IP it falls back to a SINGLE LITERAL KEY for every caller -- three sign-ins per ten seconds for the entire deployment. Behind a reverse proxy with no trusted-header configuration, that is the live behaviour.

PL-0719 reported it rather than fixing it, and gpt-architect's round-110 security review confirmed that was correct and ruled: DO NOT trust X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded, X-Real-IP or similar headers by default; a shared fallback bucket when the client IP cannot be trusted is SAFER than accepting a spoofable header that gives an attacker per-request rate-limit evasion.

SO THIS TASK IS NOT 'TURN ON FORWARDED HEADERS'. It is: decide, write down and enforce WHICH HOP MAY ASSERT A CLIENT ADDRESS, so that forwarded-client-IP semantics are enabled only where a deployment has explicitly defined that.

REQUIRED: the trusted-proxy topology is STATED IN THIS REPOSITORY -- which proxy hops are trusted, how they are identified, and what the default is when nothing is configured. The default must remain not-trusting, because that is the direction in which being wrong is survivable.
REQUIRED: an untrusted forwarded header is IGNORED, not merged, not partially honoured and not logged as if it were the client. A header from an untrusted hop is an attacker-supplied string.
REQUIRED: the direct-client case -- no proxy at all -- derives the address from the connection and is tested.
REQUIRED: the proxied case, with a configured trusted hop, derives the client address correctly and is tested, including a chain longer than one hop.
REQUIRED: A SPOOF TEST. A caller that supplies its own X-Forwarded-For must NOT be able to change which bucket it lands in. This is the test the whole task exists for and it must be seen to fail against a naive implementation.
REQUIRED: A RATE-LIMIT IDENTITY TEST. Two callers the policy should treat as distinct get distinct buckets, and one caller cannot become many by varying a header.
REQUIRED: the shared-bucket fallback remains reachable and is still correct when no trusted topology is configured. Removing it in favour of trusting something is the failure this task exists to prevent.

MUST NOT: trust any forwarded header by default, under any configuration shortcut, environment-variable convenience or development-only carve-out. MUST NOT weaken, widen or disable the rate-limit policy PL-0719 established; this task changes WHO a request is attributed to, never how many requests are allowed. MUST NOT introduce a header or parameter that lets a caller nominate its own identity for any purpose.

OUT OF SCOPE: geo-IP, IP reputation, blocklists, and any other use of a client address beyond rate-limit identity. Deriving the address correctly is this task; what else might be done with it is not.
assigned.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 110 at gpt-architect's explicit instruction in the PL-0719 security verdict: "Create a separate deployment-security task if one does not already exist: define trusted-proxy topology and client-IP derivation. Only enable forwarded-client-IP semantics when the deployment explicitly defines which proxy hop is trusted." The verdict states the follow-up does NOT block PL-0719, which is DONE.

Board searched before filing: no task names a proxy, a forwarded header or client-IP derivation in acceptance or notes. PL-0719 (DONE) owns the rate-limit POLICY and names this hazard; it is listed here as a review dependency rather than an allowed path, so this task can be read against it without reserving it.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. Active tasks are PL-0714 (.github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (apps/desktop/**, docs/LICENSING.md), PW-0602 (e2e/windows/**, .github/workflows/windows.yml) and PL-0720 (one e2e spec). None names anything under packages/auth or docs/DEPLOYMENT_TRUST.md. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts and index.ts were PL-0719's and PL-0719 is now DONE.

P1 and not P0: the current behaviour FAILS CLOSED -- a shared bucket is restrictive, not permissive -- so nothing is open today. What is missing is the topology decision, and the danger is that somebody closes the availability gap by trusting a spoofable header, which would be strictly worse than the gap.

typecheck.evidence:
npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 0 failures. npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/auth/tsconfig.json alone: exit 0.

ONE ERROR WAS CAUGHT AND IS WORTH RECORDING, because the fix is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes the vendor's advanced.ipAddress wants MUTABLE arrays, and client-ip.ts publishes readonly ones so nothing downstream can edit a trusted-hop list. better-auth.ts now copies at the boundary -- and the same helper is where `trustedProxies` is OMITTED rather than set to undefined for the direct topology. That omission is not a type nicety: the library branches on `trustedProxies.length > 0`, so an empty array selects the branch that accepts a single-valued X-Forwarded-For from anybody.
